Bayesian temperature reconstructions

Source: R/rec.bayesian.R
rec.bayesian.Rd

Reconstructs temperatures (in degrees C) from the posterior draws of a Bayesian calibration and the measured D47 of each sample. This approach is congruent with the one used in McClelland et al. (2022).

Usage

rec.bayesian(
  calModel,
  recData,
  ndraws = 10000,
  model = NULL,
  newMaterial = FALSE,
  level = 0.95,
  ...
)

Arguments

calModel

Posterior draws from cal.draws(), a result from cal.bayesian(), or a single stanfit from it.

recData

The reconstruction dataset. It needs the columns Sample, D47, and D47error (1 SD of the D47 value). If D47 is the mean of several replicates, D47error should be its standard error. Add N (number of replicates) or D47sd (SD of the replicates) to also get SD. The output of avg.replicates() has both. Mixed models also need Material, with the same labels used in the calibration.

ndraws

Number of draws used for each sample.

model

The model to use when calModel holds more than one, such as "errors".

newMaterial

For mixed models, whether the samples belong to a material that is not in the calibration. When TRUE, Material in recData is ignored. When calModel is a table of draws, get them with cal.draws(fit, newMaterial = TRUE) instead.

level

Probability covered by the interval.

...

Arguments from earlier versions (iter, mixed, postcalsamples, and MC). They are ignored.

Value

A data.frame with one row per sample. meanTemp is the posterior mean temperature (in degrees C). SE is the standard error of the temperature, propagated from D47error. SD is the SD of the temperature of a single replicate, propagated from the SD of the replicates (D47error x sqrt(N), or D47sd when N is missing). It is NA without replicate information. Both include the uncertainty in the calibration. median, lower, and upper are the posterior median and the limits of the interval, based on SE.

Details

With a flat prior on 10^6/T^2, the posterior of 10^6/T^2 for each calibration draw is normal. Its mean is (D47 - alpha) / beta and its SD is sqrt(sigma^2 + D47error^2) / beta. This function samples it directly, so no MCMC run is needed. Draws with 10^6/T^2 at or below zero are not physically possible. They are removed with a warning.

The uncertainty includes the calibration parameters, the residual SD of the calibration (sigma), and D47error. For models with measurement errors, sigma excludes the measurement error of the calibration samples. For models without them, it includes it.

Examples

# \donttest{
ds <- cal.dataset(error = "S1", nobs = 50, seed = 1)
fit <- cal.bayesian(ds, models = "errors", numSavedSteps = 1000)
#> Warning: Bulk Effective Samples Size (ESS) is too low, indicating posterior means and medians may be unreliable.
#> Running the chains for more iterations may help. See
#> https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings.html#bulk-ess
recData <- data.frame(Sample = c("A", "B"), D47 = c(0.6, 0.7), D47error = 0.01, N = 3)
rec.bayesian(fit, recData)
#>   Sample D47 D47error meanTemp        SD       SE   median    lower    upper
#> 1      A 0.6     0.01 59.42824 10.889156 8.119676 59.10102 44.24167 76.50797
#> 2      B 0.7     0.01 18.64228  7.146598 5.449535 18.49977  8.62019 29.88454
# }
